verdict.rationale: Clerk documents its own OAuth implementation. It covers scoped access for third-party apps, Dynamic Client Registration and CIMD for client registration, a standards-based device authorization grant, custom OAuth scopes, and OIDC for Enterprise SSO, so developers get standards-based OAuth/OIDC without hand-rolling the protocol. However, the specific flows the story names are not shown in the evidence. The community refresh-token complaint concerns Clerk's own session JWT refresh, not a documented OAuth refresh-token grant, so it does not dispute the capability. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of the authorization code + PKCE flow, documented OAuth refresh-token issuance and rotation, OIDC provider details (ID tokens, discovery endpoint), and independent or hands-on corroboration.
